newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa head says French rates too high.
newsitem.headline: Axa head says French rates too high.

text.p: The chairman of French insurer Axa SA Claude Bebear, said on Thursday that French interest rates were too high and holding back the expansion of small companies, which hindered employment prospects.

Bebear, interviewed on CNN television, said small businesses were being asked to pay bank interest rates of 10-12 percent even though the banks could get funding from the Bank of France at 3.5-4.0 percent.
"That's too much and that's one very strong reason why they are unable to create jobs," he said.

High interest rates and bureaucracy were the twin causes for unemployment, which caused the gloom in France. He was unsure the cuts in income tax over five years included in the government's 1997 budget would be enough to raise that gloom.

"When you talk about five years, people...want to look at what is happening next year," he said. The government's plans to introduce complementary private pension plans would be good for the insurance sector, but were long-term proposition.
Private pensions were "a good opportunity for insurance companies, but it will come slowly. In 10 years from now, the life industry will be stronger than it is now," he said.
Bebear, asked if he supported the single European currency, said the problem was not the currency, but the Maastricht convergence criteria, which he called "stupid."
It was clear deficits of countries entering the currency had to be at the same level, but the actual level itself was not important.

Axa's recent purchase of the stake that Italian insurer Generali previously held in Axa made the situation "clearer" for the market. Bebear said he had a warchest of $5 billion, but had no acquisition in mind.

"It depends on what opportunities we find. You know, you never say 'I want to buy that and that and that.' You look at different opportunities around the world and try to find the best one and grasp it," he said.

Axa was rumoured on the Paris stockmarket on Wednesday to be poised to make a public offer for rival French insurer Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP). Axa denied market talk, but not before UAP shares had shot up more than three percent. -- Paris newsroom +331 4221 5452
